solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: King's dodgy licence for boxing ring

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing as in a box, so the shuffled letters go around the king's letter
dodgy suggests something shaky or unreliable, so the letters of licence are rearranged

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch holds a dubious permit to stage boxing matches in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing ring' reads as one phrase, but 'boxing' is the containment signal and 'ring' alone is the definition. ENCICLE, the shuffled licence, wraps R.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring something is to surround it completely, a plain synonym for this verb.

clue.text: Flight executives cap expenses to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Bosses put a ceiling on spending claims up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests air travel on expenses, but it means fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight in the sense of running away is an escape, a getaway.

clue.text: Fashion introduction to Central American Queen's partner

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter

parts.note: gives its first letter
a queen is a female cat and a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A style introduced to Central America by the royal consort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests royalty, but a queen is also a female cat whose mate is a TOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashion can mean a way of doing things, and custom is an established practice or habit.

clue.text: Form of religion popular because of church support

parts.note: RE is Religious Education, a school subject taught in a form or class
in means popular, fashionable
for can mean because of, as in 'jumped for joy'
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A popular type of faith gets backing on account of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools RE is the lesson on religion, and a form is a school class, so 'Form of religion' hides the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce is to strengthen or back up, so the verb is a synonym for support.

clue.text: Toilet paper that man tears out of middle of sordid book

indicators.note: the outer pieces are built out around the inner letters, which go into the toilet word

parts.note: loo is British slang for toilet

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters

parts.note: its central two letters
FT is the Financial Times newspaper
he is the pronoun for that man
tears as a verb means rushes, which is flies

explanation.surface: A grubby tale of a man ripping up toilet paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' reads as ripping but means rushes. Loo is British slang for toilet, and the FT (Financial Times) is a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord of the Flies is William Golding's 1954 novel about stranded schoolboys.

clue.text: Author smothers lead character in horrible twist

indicators.note: to smother is to cover over, so the verb's letters surround the single letter

parts.note: to author a text is to write it

indicators.note: the lead character of a word is its first letter

parts.note: gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A novelist suffocates the hero of a grisly tale in a gruesome plot turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Author' looks like a noun but works as the verb WRITE, which takes H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and squirm the body, as in pain; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Row involving sex upset relationship

indicators.note: upset means turned over, which in a down answer flips the letters bottom to top
involving means taking in, so the oar goes around the sex word

parts.note: an oar is used to row a boat
IT is a coy term for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A quarrel about sex disturbs a relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but here it is the verb's tool, a boat paddle; 'upset' turns the whole thing upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is a quantitative relation between two amounts, a mathematical relationship.

clue.text: Run through supporter's pranks for Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words change places

parts.note: fans are supporters, and the apostrophe s makes fan's
tricks are pranks, said with the same sound as trix

explanation.surface: A football fan's practical jokes, retold in muddled Spooner style.
explanation.walkthrough: FAN'S TRICKS with the opening sounds swapped becomes TRANS FICKS, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfix is to pierce through with a spear or similar, so it means to run through.

clue.text: All and sundry cast an eye over missing article

indicators.note: cast suggests throwing something into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
missing says a letter is left out of the fodder before it is rearranged

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Everyone looks over something with the article left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the A from 'an eye over' and rearrange NEYEOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: All and sundry is an idiom meaning every person without exception.

clue.text: He is almost borne off just after course founders

definitions.text: He is almost borne off just after course founders

indicators.note: off means wrong or bad, so the letters before it are jumbled
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: on can mean just after, as in 'on arrival'

indicators.note: a ship that founders goes down, so the letters of course are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A castaway nearly carried off after his ship's course went wrong and it sank.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes Defoe's hero, shipwrecked on an island. IS BORN rearranges to ROBINS, then ON, then COURSE rearranges to CRUSOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe's hero is wrecked when his vessel sinks and is swept off to an island.

clue.text: Dismiss person with financial responsibility

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to discharge someone, especially an officer, in disgrace
second meaning: a ... handles the money in a bank or shop

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense, to sack in disgrace, is chiefly military and less familiar than the bank-teller sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word is a verb meaning to discharge in disgrace and a noun for a bank or shop employee handling money.

clue.text: Cause offence with unfashionable display of anger

parts.note: something unfashionable is out, no longer in vogue
rage is a violent show of anger

explanation.surface: Someone offends people by throwing an old-fashioned tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrage someone is to shock and offend them deeply, so the verb fits the phrase.

clue.text: Impervious academic accepts nothing

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the zero goes inside the title

parts.note: PROF is short for professor, an academic
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A stubborn scholar takes nothing on board, unmoved by anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof, as in waterproof or bulletproof, means resistant or impenetrable, as an adjective.

clue.text: Cockney's moralising talk suppresses common sense in sinister way

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold something down within, so the sense word goes inside the talk
a Cockney, a London East Ender, traditionally drops the H at the start of a word

parts.note: a homily is a sermon or moral lecture
nous is British slang for practical good sense

explanation.surface: A Londoner's preachy lecture stifles any sensible thinking, with menacing effect.
explanation.walkthrough: Without its H the homily is OMILY, which takes NOUS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominously means in a threatening manner that suggests something bad is coming; the adverb matches the phrase.

clue.text: Sore point about including worthless material in formal statement

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the junk goes inside the rearranged letters
about here means turned around and rearranged, so the letters of sore point are shuffled

parts.note: tat is British slang for cheap, tasteless goods

explanation.surface: A touchy subject is raised over some rubbish mentioned in an official declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sore point' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is simply the letters to be rearranged; tat is British slang for cheap junk.
explanation.definitionFit: A protestation is a solemn declaration or affirmation, a formal assertion of something.

clue.text: Outline foolish artist's worried about

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the worried word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: ate as in 'what's eating you' means worried
dumb means stupid or foolish
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A daft painter is anxious, and sketches out his concerns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' gives ATE, from the sense of something eating at you.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to sketch or indicate in outline, a formal synonym for this verb.

clue.text: I omit art which could be seen as impressionist

indicators.note: could be seen as means these letters might be viewed in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A painter leaving out art might be classed as an Impressionist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressionist' suggests the art movement, but an impressionist is a mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: An impressionist entertainer copies the voices and manners of others, so is a mimic.

clue.text: Person contributing to anthologies, say, is thought-provoking

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A writer whose work appears in collections is stimulating.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is only loosely 'Person'; the surface's writer contributing to anthologies supports it.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayist is a person who writes essays, often collected in anthologies.

clue.text: Wrongdoing is encapsulated by male attitude

indicators.note: encapsulated by means enclosed within, so the little word sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: demeanour is one's manner or bearing

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour is summed up by a macho attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdemeanour is a minor offence or misdeed, a synonym for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Abandon resistance having been overwhelmed by support

indicators.note: overwhelmed suggests being engulfed, so the resistance letter is swallowed by the support

parts.note: a stand is a support or base
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Giving up the fight after being outnumbered by the back-up troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To strand someone is to leave them helpless, as a castaway left on a shore.

clue.text: Person who forms strong bond with father?

parts.note: a father is an example of an elder, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A man who has a close relationship with his dad.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a father is only one example of an elder.
explanation.definitionFit: A welder joins metal pieces with a fused joint, making a very strong bond.

clue.text: He gets around number 10 to secure Gunners victory

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the outer word holds the gunners and the victory

parts.note: 10-across is CASHIER, and a cashier in a bank is a teller
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
V is short for victory, as in the V sign

explanation.surface: An Arsenal number ten player (Arsenal are the Gunners) moves around the pitch to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number 10' and 'Gunners' suggest Arsenal football club, but 10 points to the answer of 10-across, a cashier, whose synonym is a bank teller.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller is someone who journeys from place to place, so he gets around.

clue.text: Belch out smoke with rising temperature

indicators.note: rising means going upwards, which in a down answer reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: to smoke fish or meat is to cure it

explanation.surface: Smoke billows out as the temperature climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoke' suggests a fire, but it is the preserving sense, CURE, turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To eruct is a formal word for to burp, expelling gas from the stomach.

clue.text: Hill in Arizona spread to the west of river

indicators.note: what lies west of the river letter is everything before it, so only that part is kept

parts.note: butter is a spread for bread
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Something about a hill in Arizona spreading out to the west of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer west is the left, so only the letters before R in BUTTER are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A butte is an isolated flat-topped hill with steep sides, typical of the American Southwest such as Arizona.

clue.text: Praise overworked British university dons

indicators.note: to don something is to put it on, so the overused word wraps around the two abbreviations

parts.note: an overworked phrase is trite, stale from overuse

explanation.surface: An acclaim for overburdened university lecturers in Britain (dons are university teachers).
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like a noun for lecturers but works as the verb, meaning puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute is an act or statement of praise and honour, a close synonym.

clue.text: Part of franchise awarded to offshore region

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A slice of a business franchise is handed over to cover an area out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaward means towards the sea, the direction of an offshore area.

clue.text: Move round work schedule with three on vacation

parts.note: a rota is a list of who works when

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the word three loses its inside and keeps its ends

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Shifting a work timetable so that three staff are away on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn about a centre or take turns, so it means revolve or move round.

clue.text: He does perhaps start off from goal lines

definitions.text: He does perhaps start off from goal lines

indicators.note: to line something is to cover its inside, so the deer letters go around the others

parts.note: does, female deer, are an example of deer

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: gives its first letter
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A footballer in defence restarts play from the goal line, perhaps with a goal kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like a verb but is the plural of doe. The whole clue describes a defender, a player stationed by the goal line; the blog's commenter also reads FEND (ward off) inside DEER, which gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A defender is a player guarding the goal, so he often starts play from the goal area.
